ev.q: The age-adjusted death rate for stroke declined for all regions from 2001 to 2021.
Age-adjusted rates are based on the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Stroke death rates declined from 2001 through 2013 for persons living in the South (63.0 to 39.5 per 100,000 population)
Throughout the period, stroke death rates were highest in the South and lowest in the Northeast.
Age-adjusted rates are based on the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Source: National Vital Statistics System, Mortality Data, 2001–2021.
However, rates then increased through 2021 for all regions (South = 46.9, Midwest = 42.2, West = 40.0, and Northeast = 30.2).

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted rates are based on the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Deaths for stroke were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision underlying cause of death codes I60–I69.
